title: 5 resources to help dentists prescribe antibiotics responsibly
html:
Antibiotic Awareness Week is Nov. 18-24, and the American Dental Association offers multiple resources to help dentists prescribe antibiotics responsibly.

Learn more about each antibiotic stewardship resource below.

• ADA clinical practice statement: In a clinical practice statement published in The Journal of the American Dental Association, the ADA calls for dentistry to move away from a “just-in-case approach” to antibiotic prescribing to an “evidence-based, when absolutely needed model.”

• Chairside prescribing guide: This chairside tool provides antibiotic-prescribing guidance for odontogenic and selected periodontal infections in immunocompetent adults.

• New CE course: A new continuing education course on antibiotic stewardship, led by ADA President Thomas Paumier, D.D.S., will cover the risks associated with antibiotic use, the latest clinical practice guidelines for antibiotic prophylaxis, the best practices for antibiotic use in dentistry, and information dentists can use to implement an antibiotic stewardship program in their offices or clinics.

• Prosthetic joint chairside tool: This chairside tool includes a clinical flowchart to support decision-making for patients with joint replacements undergoing dental procedures.

• JADA editorial: In “Protecting Patients Beyond the Chair: Antibiotic Stewardship in Dentistry,” Dr. Paumier highlights the importance of antibiotic stewardship in dentistry and the role dental professionals play in protecting both patients and public health.

The ADA Living Guideline Program is also accepting comments through Nov. 27 on the second recommendation and set of good practice statements from a new living guideline on antibiotic prophylaxis for surgical procedures related to dental implant placement.

The draft recommendation and good practice statements address antibiotic prophylaxis for healthy patients undergoing dental implant placement surgery without simultaneous alveolar ridge or sinus augmentation. This is the second of three sets of recommendations and good practice statements to be released from the evidence-informed guideline.

The ADA invites dentists, other healthcare professionals, patients, organizations and policymakers to share their expertise and insights to help shape the guideline.

To take part, download and review the draft recommendation and good practice statements at ADA.org/guidelinecomments, register for an optional virtual listening session at 4 p.m. CST Nov. 19, and submit comments and feedback via the online form on the guideline comments webpage by Nov. 27. Attendance at the listening session is not required to provide feedback.

The ADA will review and incorporate feedback from the public comment period into the final recommendation and good practice statements, which are expected to be published in spring 2027.

The guideline is part of the ADA’s ongoing collaboration with the University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine on living guidelines. A previous living guideline addressed early oral cancer detection.

Established in 2025, the ADA Living Guideline Program seeks to provide oral healthcare providers and patients with more frequent evidence-informed recommendations to advance oral and overall health. The program upholds the methodological rigor of traditional guidelines, but living guidelines are updated as new evidence becomes available.

Those with questions about the antibiotic prophylaxis guideline can email guidelineprogram@ada.org.
